structure.title: Adventures interpreted
structure.text: Part One follows the knight and Sancho through encounters transformed by the books and expectations they bring to them.

structure.title: A reputation in circulation
structure.text: Part Two makes the travellers' known stories part of new encounters. Other people can now use their reputations to arrange adventures for them.

people.name: Don Quixote
people.text: A poor Spanish gentleman who has read so many romances of chivalry that he renames himself a knight and sets out to right the world's wrongs.

people.name: Sancho Panza
people.text: A shrewd, talkative farmer who rides beside the knight on a donkey, half believing the promise of an island to govern.

people.name: Dulcinea
people.text: A farm girl from a nearby village, whom Don Quixote turns in his imagination into the peerless lady of his chivalry.

context.title: Chivalric stories
context.text: Quixote expects a world of quests, enchanted threats, and honourable service. Everyday encounters keep resisting the roles he assigns them.
context.takeaway: You need the expectations, not a reading list.

context.title: Narrators and sources
context.text: Cervantes plays with authorship, translation, and the reliability of the story's transmission. The telling itself becomes part of the comedy.
context.takeaway: Ask who claims authority for an episode.

notice.text: Follow changes in the companions' language.
notice.why: Their friendship alters how each describes the world.
Being correct about an illusion does not guarantee kindness.

opening: A man reads so many tales of chivalry that he equips himself as a knight and rides out to put the world right. His neighbour Sancho follows, partly for the promised rewards and partly because abandoning him becomes difficult. Inns, labourers, and windmills keep refusing the parts assigned to them. Cervantes makes the collisions hilarious, but the pair's companionship gradually complicates the laughter: the man who misunderstands almost everything can still see possibilities of courage and generosity that more sensible people have stopped expecting.
